Work contexts

Kindergarten through secondary education administrators work in public or private elementary and secondary schools, handling curriculum and teaching supervision, staff and student affairs, budgets, and operational support. They work year-round and do not take time off when students are on vacation.
Work locations: mainly school offices, with management by walking around in classrooms, activity areas, and community locations.
Main objects: curricula and teaching, teaching staff, student affairs, budgets, school buildings and operational support, and reports to competent authorities.
Handovers are needed with teachers, parents, communities, suppliers, and education authorities.
Work hours: mostly full-time and year-round; often attend parent meetings and school events in evenings or on weekends.
Risks mainly arise from prolonged intensive communication and emergency pressure, and the psychological burden and accountability associated with unexpected safety incidents.
Tools and information: student enrollment and achievement management systems, office and budget software, regulatory and policy databases, and emergency and safety checklists.

Safety boundaries: only trained, qualified, and authorized personnel may implement decisions involving protection of minors, student records, discipline, and personnel under applicable regulations and procedures.

How AI may change the work of kindergarten through secondary education administrators

AI and digital tools can assist with organizing achievement and attendance data, drafting reports and notices, drafting schedules and budget calculations, and information searches. They cannot replace professional judgments on curricula and teaching, handling of student discipline and safety incidents, staff assessment and personnel decisions, or tradeoffs in budgets and resource allocation, and do not bear administrative or legal responsibility for school operations.

items.title: How to choose training, qualifications, and materials

paragraphs: Read degree, teacher qualification, teaching-duration, and management experience requirements in recruitment or appointment announcements individually. Flexibility on one requirement does not mean the others can be substituted.
The suggested work samples and seven-day experience on this page are for career exploration only, and do not establish eligibility, appointment, or hiring.
Teacher qualifications and principal appointments can only be obtained by qualified individuals under local rules and competent authority procedures.
Exercises on this page use fictional materials and do not represent any actual school, teachers, students, or decisions.

Typical U.S. principals have a master's degree in educational administration/leadership and several years of teaching experience; 62/27/10 educational feedback does not establish a uniform five-year requirement. Most states require public principals to hold an administrator license; private principals do not require a state-issued license.

China's 2026 measures apply to public school leadership teams, generally requiring a bachelor's degree, corresponding teacher qualifications, and a professional technical position. Check relaxations for education stages/regions, exceptionally outstanding candidates, or special needs separately; check private schools and ordinary administrative roles separately.

Public school principals generally require 5 years of educational and teaching experience. Internal promotion to the top position requires 2 years as a deputy or 3 years in middle management, with successful training; in exceptional cases, training may be completed within 1 year after promotion. Check Article 7 relaxations separately; degrees/experience do not directly confer appointment.

entries: Day 1: can you accurately identify a provision's applicability and exceptions rather than merely copying keywords?

subject.name: Kindergarten through secondary education administrators
subject.summary: Under U.S. O*NET-SOC 11-9032.00, plan, direct, or coordinate academic, administrative, and auxiliary activities in kindergartens, elementary schools, or secondary schools: supervise curricula and teaching according to school objectives and applicable regulations, develop teachers, handle student affairs and home-school communication, prepare and implement budgets, arrange school buildings and operational support, and take responsibility for school operational outcomes.
